- If sentiment is positive (≥0.4) in recent history, reduce forecasted peaks and avoid over-optimistic spikes.  
- If forecast shows early sharp upward moves (e.g., >+3% from prior day), cap or dampen the next 3–5 days’ forecast to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a spike, model should adjust downward in subsequent days — especially if sentiment remains neutral or negative.  
- When true price drops sharply after a forecast peak, reduce forecasted decline rate by 10–20% to avoid underestimating volatility.  
- If forecast is consistently higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, apply a 5–10% downward bias to next forecast horizon.  
- If sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), assume no directional bias — use historical mean or simple moving average for correction.  
- If forecast shows strong upward trend but true outcome is flat or declining, reduce forecast slope by 20–30% for next 7 days.
